Investing.com -- Intermediate Capital Group () reported fee-related earnings of £199 million, or 68 pence per share, for the first half of fiscal 2027, up 18% YoY. Management fees rose 12% YoY to £374 million. The company’s assets under management reached $145 billion, with fee-earning AUM of $90 billion, up 9% over the last twelve months.

The firm recently closed its Europe IX fund at €12 billion, which it described as the largest structured capital fund ever raised globally. The fund was materially oversubscribed. ICG raised $7.6 billion in the six-month period, with net additions to fee-earning AUM of $4.7 billion. The company recorded performance fee income of £24 million and realized performance fees of £18 million.

"ICG is in an exciting period of inflexion," said Benoît Durteste, CIO and CEO. "We are seeing our focus on long-term investment performance rather than short-term asset gathering increasingly recognised by institutional clients."

ICG announced a target of maintaining zero net debt over the medium term. The company reported net debt of £93 million, down from £113 million at fiscal year-end 2026, with total available liquidity of £1.4 billion. Group operating cash flow was £219 million for the period.

IT declared an interim dividend of 29.0 pence per share, up from 27.7 pence in the first half of fiscal 2026. ICG reaffirmed its progressive dividend policy and stated that after funding growth opportunities, excess capital will be returned to shareholders.

The company’s balance sheet portfolio stood at £2.6 billion. Over the past five years, ICG’s fee-related earnings per share has grown at an annualized rate of 28%.
